Fit the monthly share-of-annual-runoff model

Source: R/wet_share_fit.R
wet_share_fit.Rd

Splits annual runoff into months. Three methods, each fitted on the same complete stations:

Usage

wet_share_fit(
  d,
  static = c("elev", "e_km", "n_km"),
  method = c("regression", "donor", "blend"),
  k = 5
)

Arguments

d

data.frame with observed shares share_01 to share_12, the monthly predictors ppt_MM, tave_MM, aet_MM, and the static columns. A station missing any of them is left out, whatever the method.

static

Predictors used in every month, one value per station, each with its own coefficient in each month ("regression"), or the space the donors are found in ("donor"). The snow predictors scored in #16 enter here: static = c("elev", "e_km", "n_km", "snowmelt_doy_50", "swe_max"), the upstream means of wet_snow_normals().

method

"regression", "donor" or "blend".

k

Donors per watershed ("donor" and "blend"), capped at the number of stations.

Value

A wet_share_fit object. For "regression", list(coef, terms, static, n, method), where coef is a 12-row matrix of coefficients (intercept first) by month. For "donor", the stations' scaled predictors x, their standard deviations sd and observed shares. For "blend", both fits, as regression and donor.

Details

  • "regression": Chapman et al. (2018) fit one regression per month of each month's share of the annual total. Here the response is the observed share (from monthly volumes, wet_station_monthly()) and the predictors, fixed in advance, are upstream means: that month's precipitation, temperature and AET plus any static columns (by default elevation and BC Albers easting and northing).

  • "donor" (#102): a watershed takes the inverse-distance mean of the observed shares of its k nearest stations in the space of the static predictors, each divided by the stations' standard deviation. Distance weights are 1 / (d + 1e-6 * median(d)); a station at distance 0 takes the whole weight, so a station predicts its own shares.

  • "blend": the equal-weight mean of the two.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(elev = runif(30, 200, 2000), e_km = runif(30, 900, 1800), n_km = runif(30, 400, 1500))
for (m in 1:12) {
  d[[sprintf("ppt_%02d", m)]] <- runif(30, 20, 200)
  d[[sprintf("tave_%02d", m)]] <- runif(30, -15, 20)
  d[[sprintf("aet_%02d", m)]] <- runif(30, 0, 100)
  # a freshet that comes later and larger at higher elevation
  d[[sprintf("share_%02d", m)]] <- 1 + (m %in% 5:7) * d$elev / 500
}
tot <- rowSums(d[sprintf("share_%02d", 1:12)])
d[sprintf("share_%02d", 1:12)] <- d[sprintf("share_%02d", 1:12)] / tot
new <- d[1:2, ]
new$elev <- c(300, 1900)
# the low watershed gets less of its year in May-July than the high one
round(wet_share_predict(wet_share_fit(d, method = "donor"), new)[, 5:7], 3)
#>      share_05 share_06 share_07
#> [1,]    0.128    0.128    0.128
#> [2,]    0.202    0.202    0.202
